title: Refactor block headers for edit-mode reorder behavior
description: Restructure block header rendering into discrete tap regions and wire block reordering from the outer block list, including hiding drag affordances while search filtering is active.
acceptance_criteria: Block headers no longer use one row-wide collapse button in Edit mode.
The center heading/chevron region is the only collapse toggle target.
The outer block list supports `.onMove` against the unfiltered block array when search is empty.
Drag handles are unavailable while `searchText` is non-empty, without affecting rename availability.

handoff_summary.completed: All four acceptance criteria satisfied: (1) block header is no longer a row-wide button; (2) only the center heading+chevron region toggles collapse; (3) .onMove wired against plan.blocks via Array.move semantics when search is empty; (4) drag handles suppressed via editMode environment when searchText is non-empty while pencil rename button remains available. Rename alert updated to also block == in headings per spec validation rules. Build succeeded with no errors.
handoff_summary.risks: Low. The .environment(\.editMode, .constant(...)) approach controls drag-handle visibility cleanly. The .onMove offset math is correct when search is empty because visibleBlocks == plan.blocks in that state. If a future bead allows reorder while search is active, the index-translation problem noted in the spec will need addressing then.
handoff_summary.next_action: Hand off to tester agent to verify block header tap-target isolation, drag-handle visibility gating, and rename alert == validation.
handoff_summary.conflict_risks: None. Only MealPlanDetailView.swift was touched; no sibling beads claim this file.
handoff_summary.design_decisions: Used .environment(\.editMode, .constant(...)) on the List rather than injecting a full @Environment(\.editMode) binding, to keep isEditMode as the single source of truth and avoid leaking system EditMode into item-row behavior. Used Array.move(fromOffsets:toOffset:) directly on plan.blocks in the .onMove closure rather than delegating to moveBlock(from:to:), because Array.move has the correct SwiftUI offset semantics (toOffset is insert-before in original array) whereas moveBlock(from:to:) uses remove-then-insert-at semantics that would require manual offset adjustment.
handoff_summary.test_coverage_notes: No tests modified (developer role; test execution is tester's responsibility). Tester should verify: tap on pencil does not toggle collapse; tap on heading/chevron does toggle collapse; drag handle absent when searchText non-empty; drag handle present when edit mode active and search empty; Save disabled for empty and ==-containing names; == error message visible in alert.
handoff_summary.known_limitations: Reordering while search is active is intentionally disabled. If the user wants to reorder, they must clear the search field first.

conflict_risks: None. Only MealPlanDetailView.swift was touched; no sibling beads claim this file.

execution_history.summary: Refactored MealPlanDetailView block headers and wired block reordering. The row-wide collapse Button is replaced by an HStack of three discrete tap regions: leading pencil Button (edit mode only, opens rename alert), center collapse Button (heading + chevron only), and trailing system drag handle (injected by .onMove). Added .onMove on the outer ForEach wired to plan.blocks.move(fromOffsets:toOffset:) + persistPlan. The List's editMode environment is set active only when isEditMode && searchText.isEmpty, so drag handles are hidden while searching. The rename alert also now validates against == in block names with an inline error message.
